facts_of_case: The applicant-appellant seeks maintenance pendente lite and litigation expenses. The respondent-husband earns Rs.12,000/- per month and has a bank balance earning interest.

legal_principles.principle: When the court intervenes under the Hindu Marriage Act, it has the power to grant permanent alimony or maintenance.
legal_principles.held: It undoubtedly has the power to grant permanent alimony or maintenance, if that power is invoked at that time. It also retains the power subsequently to be invoked on application by a party entitled to relief.
cited_cases: Gurmit Kaur vs Buta Singh, (2009) X SCC Y
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to situations where the court intervenes under the Hindu Marriage Act

legal_principles.principle: The expression 'at the time of passing any decree' in Section 25 encompasses all kinds of decrees, including restitution of conjugal rights and declaring a marriage null and void.
legal_principles.held: When the legislature has used such wide expression as 'at the time of passing of any decree,' it encompasses within the expression all kinds of decrees such as restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9, declaring marriage null and void
keywords: declaring a marriage null and void
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — applies to situations where the court is considering granting alimony or maintenance

outcome.final_order: Maintenance pendente lite and litigation expenses granted to the applicant-appellant.
